title: Clock-ins and clock-outs: attendance in one click

s01.narration: A paper attendance book, and chasing down who came in when at the end of the month? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and today I'll show you clock-ins and clock-outs.

s02.narration: People clock in and out with a single click, on the web or at an attendance terminal. And you get attendance that's ready to use for payroll.

s03.narration: I'll show you the setup, everyday clocking in, and the manager's view. You'll find the module in the left menu under Attendance.

s04.narration: Let's start with the setup. At the bottom of the left menu, I click Attendance settings.

s05.narration: In the Changes section, you let people correct their own attendance. I recommend keeping approval by an attendance approver switched on.

s06.narration: Closing timesheets makes sure approvers close the timesheet every month. Here, between the first and the fourth day of the following month.

s07.narration: Automatic breaks add the lunch break based on working hours, so people don't have to clock it.

s08.narration: The Events tab holds the departure types, such as lunch, a break, or a doctor's visit.

s09.narration: For each one, you decide whether it counts as work and where people see it, for example on the terminal or on a desktop.

s10.narration: If you have an attendance terminal, you add it in the Terminals tab. You assign card or chip numbers to people in Attendance cards.

s11.narration: Now for an ordinary day. You get to work in the morning and find the Attendance widget on your Dashboard.

s12.narration: The widget shows whether you're at work, how much you've worked today, and your balance up to today.

s13.narration: I click Clock in. Sloneek instantly saves the time you arrived.

s14.narration: The status has switched to At work, and the button has changed to Clock out. Your time is counted from this moment.

s15.narration: You'll find the details in the Attendance module. I'll open it straight from the widget.

s16.narration: In the Me view, you see the whole month. Each day has a timeline: work in green, breaks in orange, and time off in grey.

s17.narration: On the right is the day's detail: the daily goal, how much you've worked, the balance, and a list of segments.

s18.narration: Below it is the month summary with the total balance, so you see right away whether you have overtime or are short of hours.

s19.narration: Forgot to clock in? With the Add segment button, you can fill in the missing time, even after the fact.

s20.narration: You choose the segment type and the time from and to. Your manager then approves the change. I'll close the dialog now.

s21.narration: When you leave, you click Clock out. The menu also offers interruptions, such as lunch, a break, or a doctor's visit.

s22.narration: At the end of the day, I choose End of shift. The At work segment now has both a start and an end.

s23.narration: And how does a manager see it? In the Team view, they have their people's attendance listed one below the other.

s24.narration: An admin can pick any team; a manager only sees their own. In Filters, they can show, for example, only errors or approval requests.

s25.narration: The manager finds requests to change attendance in Approvals.

s26.narration: In the Attendance tab, they see both the original and the new value, and approve or reject the change with one click.

s27.narration: You'll find attendance data for payroll and checks in Custom reports, among the pre-made reports.

s28.narration: I'll open the Overview of clock-ins and clock-outs, with every clock-in and clock-out for the chosen period.

s29.narration: For each record, you see the start, the end, the duration, and how it was entered, such as web or terminal. You can export the report to Excel.

s30.narration: And that's it. You now know how to set up attendance, clock in and out, and keep track of your whole team.

s31.narration: A final tip: on the Dashboard, you'll also find the Team attendance widget. It shows each team member's balance up to today.

s32.narration: If something doesn't work, check the Help Center. Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
